query: Could you show me, for each city, what time these programs open and close on Mondays and Tuesdays, along with the typical, total, and highest ZIP code values for those locations, broken out by your ZIP code category?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.monhouropen,
    t4.programzipcode,
    t4.tuehouropen,
    t5.tuehourclose,
    t6.programcity,
    t6.monhourclose,
    CASE 
      WHEN t4.programzipcode > 11600 THEN 'Very High ZIP'
      WHEN t4.programzipcode > 11200 THEN 'High ZIP'
      ELSE 'Standard ZIP'
    END as category
  FROM `Department for the Aging (NYC Aging) - All Contracted Providers_aging_contracted_providers_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Department for the Aging (NYC Aging) - All Contracted Providers_aging_contracted_providers` t2 ON t1.dfta_id = t2.dfta_id
  INNER JOIN `Department for the Aging (NYC Aging) - All Contracted Providers_caregiver_program_hours` t3 ON t1.programname = t3.programname
  INNER JOIN `Department for the Aging (NYC Aging) - All Contracted Providers_aging_contract_providers_locations` t4 ON t1.programaddress = t4.programaddress
  INNER JOIN `Department for the Aging (NYC Aging) - All Contracted Providers_aging_contract_providers_info_1` t5 ON t2.programphone = t5.programphone
  INNER JOIN `Department for the Aging (NYC Aging) - All Contracted Providers_aging_contract_providers_info` t6 ON t2.location1 = t6.location1
  WHERE t6.programcity IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  programcity,
  monhouropen,
  tuehouropen,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(programzipcode) as avg_value,
  SUM(programzipcode) as total_value,
  MAX(programzipcode) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  programcity,
  monhouropen,
  tuehouropen,
  category

SELECT t3.doing_business_as_dba, t4.qualify_alcohol, SUM(t4.sidewalk_dimensions_length) AS total, AVG(t4.sidewalk_dimensions_length) AS average, COUNT(*) AS count FROM `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_application_records` t1
INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_permit_applications` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_open_applications` t3 ON t1.globalid = t3.globalid
INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_historic_open_restaurant_data` t4 ON t1.business_address = t4.business_address
INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_seating_applications` t5 ON t2.legal_business_name = t5.legal_business_name GROUP BY t3.doing_business_as_dba, t4.qualify_alcohol

query: Could you show me, for each restaurant that has sidewalk seating, a breakdown by street address and the name they operate under, including whether they’re allowed to serve alcohol, how wide their sidewalk space is on average (along with the total and maximum widths), and how many applications fall into each size category of sidewalk area?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.globalid,
    t1.business_address,
    t1.time_of_submission,
    t3.globalid AS t3_globalid,
    t3.doing_business_as_dba,
    t4.business_address AS t4_business_address,
    t4.sidewalk_dimensions_width,
    t4.qualify_alcohol,
    t5.seating_interest_sidewalk,
    CASE 
      WHEN t4.sidewalk_dimensions_width > 15 THEN 'large'
      WHEN t4.sidewalk_dimensions_width > 8 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'small'
    END as category
  FROM `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_application_records` t1
  INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_permit_applications` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_open_applications` t3 ON t1.globalid = t3.globalid
  INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_historic_open_restaurant_data` t4 ON t1.business_address = t4.business_address
  INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_seating_applications` t5 ON t2.legal_business_name = t5.legal_business_name
  WHERE t5.seating_interest_sidewalk = 'sidewalk'
)
SELECT 
  business_address,
  doing_business_as_dba,
  qualify_alcohol,
  seating_interest_sidewalk,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(sidewalk_dimensions_width) as avg_value,
  SUM(sidewalk_dimensions_width) as total_value,
  MAX(sidewalk_dimensions_width) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  business_address,
  doing_business_as_dba,
  qualify_alcohol,
  seating_interest_sidewalk,
  category

query: Can you pull the top 50 restaurants that have outdoor seating specifically on the sidewalk, showing each place’s official registered name and any trade name they use, whether they’re in or tied to a landmark building or district, their full street address, what kind of liquor or service license they hold, and for each one how many separate sidewalk seating entries they have, along with the total and average length of their sidewalk seating areas, sorted from the largest total sidewalk space to the smallest, excluding any that don’t have a positive total length?
sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.legal_business_name,
    t3.doing_business_as_dba,
    t3.landmark_district_or_building,
    t4.business_address,
    t4.sla_license_type,
    t4.sidewalk_dimensions_length,
    t5.legal_business_name,
    t5.seating_interest_sidewalk
  FROM `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_application_records` t1
  INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_permit_applications` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_open_applications` t3 ON t1.globalid = t3.globalid
  INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_historic_open_restaurant_data` t4 ON t1.business_address = t4.business_address
  INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_seating_applications` t5 ON t2.legal_business_name = t5.legal_business_name
  WHERE t5.seating_interest_sidewalk = 'sidewalk'
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    legal_business_name,
    doing_business_as_dba,
    landmark_district_or_building,
    business_address,
    sla_license_type,
    seating_interest_sidewalk,
    SUM(sidewalk_dimensions_length) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(sidewalk_dimensions_length) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY 
    legal_business_name,
    doing_business_as_dba,
    landmark_district_or_building,
    business_address,
    sla_license_type,
    seating_interest_sidewalk
)
SELECT 
  legal_business_name,
  doing_business_as_dba,
  landmark_district_or_building,
  business_address,
  sla_license_type,
  seating_interest_sidewalk,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE total > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 50

sql:
WITH base_data AS (SELECT t1.objectid, t1.globalid, t1.business_address, t2.objectid, t2.legal_business_name, t3.globalid AS t3_globalid, t4.business_address AS t4_business_address, t3.doing_business_as_dba, t4.sidewalk_dimensions_length, t5.seating_interest_sidewalk FROM `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_application_records` t1
INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_permit_applications` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
INNER JOIN `Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_open_applications` t3 ON t1.globalid = t3.globalid

query: Can you show me up to five of the most recent tax prep locations for each provider, including who’s running the service, when they opened, the main service type or program code, any extra details or comments, the borough or general area, the full street address, whether they’re open on Fridays, and if they can help with amended tax returns?
sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (SELECT t3.providername, t3.opendateiso, t3.s1, t3.notes, t5.l1, t5.mappedaddress, t5.fridayopen, t5.amendedreturn, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.providername ORDER BY t3.opendateiso DESC) as row_num FROM `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites_1` t1
INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_2` t2 ON t1.sitekey = t2.sitekey
INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites` t3 ON t1.sitename = t3.sitename
INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations` t4 ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_1` t5 ON t4.building = t5.building WHERE t5.showonmap = 'Yes') SELECT providername, opendateiso, s1, notes, l1, mappedaddress, fridayopen, amendedreturn FROM ranked_data WHERE row_num <= 5

query: Could you show me a breakdown of each tax prep location, including the name of the site, who runs it, whether people need an appointment or can just walk in, the full street address, and whether it’s open on Fridays? I’d also like those locations grouped by how early or late they open on Fridays, along with how many entries there are for each group and the average, total, and latest Friday opening time for each site.
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t1.sitename, t3.sitename, t1.ifridayopen, t1.apptorwalkin, t3.providername, t5.mappedaddress, t5.fridayopen, CASE WHEN t1.ifridayopen > 15 THEN 'Late Opening' WHEN t1.ifridayopen > 10 THEN 'Midday Opening' ELSE 'Early Opening' END as category FROM `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites_1` t1
INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_2` t2 ON t1.sitekey = t2.sitekey
INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites` t3 ON t1.sitename = t3.sitename
INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations` t4 ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_1` t5 ON t4.building = t5.building WHERE t1.ifridayopen IS NOT NULL) SELECT sitename, providername, apptorwalkin, mappedaddress, fridayopen, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(ifridayopen) as avg_value, SUM(ifridayopen) as total_value, MAX(ifridayopen) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY sitename, providername, apptorwalkin, mappedaddress, fridayopen, category

query: Show, for each building in the NYC Free Tax Prep Sites data, the three most recent records based on the open date, including the main site identifier, the open date, the building, whether they provide individual taxpayer identification number services, the first-level location or unit, and the full mapped address, along with the ranking within each building and the ranking within each individual taxpayer identification number group.
sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.s1,
    t3.opendateiso,
    t4.building,
    t4.itin,
    t5.building,
    t5.l1,
    t5.mappedaddress,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t5.building 
      ORDER BY t3.opendateiso DESC
    ) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t4.itin 
      ORDER BY t3.opendateiso
    ) AS dense_rank
  FROM `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_2` t2 ON t1.sitekey = t2.sitekey
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites` t3 ON t1.sitename = t3.sitename
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations` t4 ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_1` t5 ON t4.building = t5.building
)
SELECT 
  s1,
  opendateiso,
  building,
  itin,
  l1,
  mappedaddress,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 3

query: Could you list the top 50 free tax prep locations with the highest combined activity or usage score, showing for each one the site’s name, where it’s located (including its street or building info and general area), and the coordinates you have for it, along with how many matching records you found there, the total of that usage score, and the average value per record?
sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.sitename,
    t1.sitekey,
    t2.sitekey AS t2_sitekey,
    t2.latitude,
    t2.longitude,
    t3.sitename AS t3_sitename,
    t3.s1,
    t4.latitude AS t4_latitude,
    t4.longitude AS t4_longitude,
    t4.building AS t4_building,
    t5.building,
    t5.l1,
    t5.xcoordinate
  FROM `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_2` t2 ON t1.sitekey = t2.sitekey
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites` t3 ON t1.sitename = t3.sitename
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations` t4 ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_1` t5 ON t4.building = t5.building
  WHERE t3.s1 IS NOT NULL
), aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    sitename,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    building,
    l1,
    SUM(xcoordinate) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(xcoordinate) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY sitename, latitude, longitude, building, l1
)
SELECT 
  sitename,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  building,
  l1,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE count >= 1
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 50

query: Can you show me, for each high school, the top five entries with the highest rate of students going on to college or careers, including the school’s ID, name, fax number, how many ninth-grade special education seats they offer, and how many general education applicants there are per ninth-grade seat?
sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.dbn,
    t2.dbn,
    t1.school_name,
    t3.school_name,
    t1.fax_number,
    t4.fax_number,
    t3.seats9swd5,
    t4.college_career_rate,
    t6.grade9geapplicantsperseat8,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.dbn ORDER BY t4.college_career_rate DESC) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.school_name ORDER BY t6.grade9geapplicantsperseat8) AS dense_rank
  FROM `2017 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2017` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn

sql: SELECT t5.site, SUM(CASE WHEN t5.senate_district = 11.0 THEN t5.congressional_district ELSE 0 END) AS total_cd_in_senate_11, t2.councildist, t3.ntaname, t4.dsny_section, t6.hours, t7.email FROM `node_1` t1 INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_sites_directory_1` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory_1` t3 ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_center_locations` t4 ON t1.address = t4.address INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_sites_directory` t5 ON t2.site = t5.site INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory_2` t6 ON t3.phone = t6.phone INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory` t7 ON t4.bin = t7.bin GROUP BY t5.site, t2.councildist, t3.ntaname, t4.dsny_section, t6.hours, t7.email

query: Could you list the top 50 donation locations with the highest combined district number, including each place’s name, what kinds of items they accept, which state senate district they’re in, and how many matching records you found for each, only keeping spots that have published operating hours and some specified types of donations?
sql:
WITH raw_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.objectid,
    t1.latitude,
    t1.longitude,
    t1.address,
    t2.objectid AS t2_objectid,
    t2.site,
    t3.latitude AS t3_latitude,
    t3.longitude AS t3_longitude,
    t3.phone,
    t4.bin,
    t4.address AS t4_address,
    t5.site AS t5_site,
    t5.categoriesaccepted,
    t6.phone AS t6_phone,
    t6.hours,
    t7.bin AS t7_bin,
    t7.email,
    t5.senate_district
  FROM `node_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_sites_directory_1` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory_1` t3 ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_center_locations` t4 ON t1.address = t4.address
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_sites_directory` t5 ON t2.site = t5.site
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory_2` t6 ON t3.phone = t6.phone
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory` t7 ON t4.bin = t7.bin
  WHERE t5.categoriesaccepted IS NOT NULL
), filtered AS (
  SELECT 
    objectid,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    address,
    t2_objectid,
    site,
    t3_latitude,
    t3_longitude,
    phone,
    bin,
    t4_address,
    t5_site,
    categoriesaccepted,
    t6_phone,
    hours,
    t7_bin,
    email,
    senate_district
  FROM raw_data
  WHERE hours IS NOT NULL
), aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    site,
    categoriesaccepted,
    senate_district,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    SUM(senate_district) AS total
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY site, categoriesaccepted, senate_district
)
SELECT 
  site,
  categoriesaccepted,
  senate_district,
  count,
  total
FROM aggregated
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 50

query: Could you give me a breakdown of each high school, including its name, how many students are enrolled, the best phone number to reach the main office, the school’s official website, how many different academic programs it offers, and what kinds of clubs or other after‑school activities are available?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.school_name,
    t3.total_students,
    t4.phone_number,
    t5.website,
    t6.number_programs,
    t6.extracurricular_activities,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.total_students > 1000 THEN 'large'
      WHEN t3.total_students > 500 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'small'
    END as category
  FROM `2014 - 2015 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `2014 - 2015 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN `2014 - 2015 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2014_2015` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN `2014 - 2015 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2` t4 ON t1.phone_number = t4.phone_number
  INNER JOIN `2014 - 2015 DOE High School Directory_nyc_high_school_directory` t5 ON t1.website = t5.website
  INNER JOIN `2014 - 2015 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_3` t6 ON t2.fax_number = t6.fax_number
  WHERE t3.total_students IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  school_name,
  website,
  number_programs,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(total_students) as avg_value,
  SUM(total_students) as total_value,
  MAX(total_students) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  school_name,
  website,
  number_programs,
  category

query: For each disqualified entity in the Local Law 44 disqualified entities list, show the entity name, the street address it matches in the disqualified property owners records, the last name of the primary individual, the matched entity name from the related entities list, the matched street address from the property owners records, the corresponding primary individual’s last name from the disqualified individuals list, the last name of any third listed principal from the property owners records, the country associated with that individual, and the first listed individual title from the node 6 records, limited to the top ranked five matches per entity based on officer equivalent 2 and using the dense rank by primary last name and officer equivalent 5.
sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.entity_name,
    t1.street_address,
    t1.owner_officer_1_last_name,
    t2.entity_name AS t2_entity_name,
    t3.street_address AS t3_street_address,
    t4.owner_officer_1_last_name AS t4_owner_officer_1_last_name,
    t3.owner_officer_3_last_name,
    t4.country,
    t6.individual_title_1,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.entity_name ORDER BY t3.officer_equivalent_2 DESC) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t4.owner_officer_1_last_name ORDER BY t6.officer_equivalent_5) AS dense_rank
  FROM `Local Law 44 Disqualified List_disqualified_entities_list_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Local Law 44 Disqualified List_disqualified_entities_list` t2 ON t1.entity_name = t2.entity_name
  INNER JOIN `Local Law 44 Disqualified List_disqualified_property_owners` t3 ON t1.street_address = t3.street_address
  INNER JOIN `Local Law 44 Disqualified List_disqualified_individuals_list` t4 ON t1.owner_officer_1_last_name = t4.owner_officer_1_last_name
  INNER JOIN `Local Law 44 Disqualified List_disqualified_contractors_list` t5 ON t2.owner_officer_1_first_name = t5.owner_officer_1_first_name
  INNER JOIN `node_6` t6 ON t5.postcode = t6.postcode
) 
SELECT 
  entity_name,
  street_address,
  owner_officer_1_last_name,
  t2_entity_name,
  t3_street_address,
  t4_owner_officer_1_last_name,
  owner_officer_3_last_name,
  country,
  individual_title_1,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM ranked 
WHERE rank <= 5

query: Could you list the top five Greenstreet locations within each state senate district, including the district number, the relevant committee or commission they fall under, the associated city council district, the name of each site, the type of Greenstreet it is, and the organization responsible for it?
sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.nys_senate,
    t3.commission,
    t5.councildis,
    t5.propname,
    t5.gstype,
    t5.organizati,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.nys_senate ORDER BY t5.councildis DESC) AS row_num
  FROM `ARCHIVE - Greenstreets_greenstreets_site_information` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN `ARCHIVE - Greenstreets_greenstreets_senate_commissions` t3 ON t1.system = t3.system
  INNER JOIN `ARCHIVE - Greenstreets_greenstreets_park_locations` t4 ON t2.omppropid = t4.omppropid
  INNER JOIN `ARCHIVE - Greenstreets_greenstreets_locations_nyc` t5 ON t4.global_id = t5.global_id
  WHERE t5.gstype = 'Greenstreet'
)
SELECT 
  nys_senate,
  commission,
  councildis,
  propname,
  gstype,
  organizati
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 5

query: For each neighborhood, can you break down the different types of social services offered, show whether they include meal or food support, and then summarize how many locations there are in each category along with the average, total, and highest funding levels for those services, but only counting sites with a confirmed street address?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.fixed_address,
    t3.state_senate_district,
    t4.city,
    t4.site_budget,
    t5.service_taxonomy,
    t6.serves_food,
    CASE 
      WHEN t4.site_budget > 500000 THEN 'High Budget'
      WHEN t4.site_budget > 100000 THEN 'Medium Budget'
      ELSE 'Low Budget'
    END as category
  FROM `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_sites` t1
  INNER JOIN `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_sites_3` t2 ON t1.site_id = t2.site_id
  INNER JOIN `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_sites_1` t3 ON t1.site_name = t3.site_name
  INNER JOIN `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_sites_2` t4 ON t1.address_1 = t4.address_1
  INNER JOIN `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_social_service_contract_sites` t5 ON t1.contract_id = t5.contract_id
  INNER JOIN `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_locations` t6 ON t2.latitude = t6.latitude AND t2.longitude = t6.longitude 
  WHERE t3.fixed_address = TRUE
)
SELECT 
  city,
  service_taxonomy,
  serves_food,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(site_budget) as avg_value,
  SUM(site_budget) as total_value,
  MAX(site_budget) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  city,
  service_taxonomy,
  serves_food,
  category

sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.contract_id,
    t1.site_name,
    t1.address_1,
    t1.capacity,
    t3.site_name AS t3_site_name,
    t3.fixed_address,
    t4.address_1 AS t4_address_1,
    t4.site_budget,

    t5.service_taxonomy,

  INNER JOIN `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_sites_3` t2 ON t1.site_id = t2.site_id

  INNER JOIN `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_sites_2` t4 ON t1.address_1 = t4.address_1

sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (

  INNER JOIN `DOE High School Directory 2013-2014_high_school_directory` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn

  WHERE t3.progcount IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t2_printed_name,
  t4_printed_name,
  t4_alphabetic_name_long,
  t5_alphabetic_name_long,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(progcount) AS avg_value,
  SUM(progcount) AS total_value,
  MAX(progcount) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data

  t4_printed_name,
  t4_alphabetic_name_long,
  t5_alphabetic_name_long,

sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.manhattan_condominium_property_address,

  FROM `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables_2` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables` t2 ON t1.manhattan_condominium_property_condo_section = t2.manhattan_condominium_property_condo_section
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_income_1` t3 ON t1.manhattan_condominium_property_address = t3.manhattan_condominium_property_address
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_income` t4 ON t1.manhattan_condominium_property_boro_block_lot = t4.manhattan_condominium_property_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables_3` t5 ON t2.latitude = t5.latitude AND t2.longitude = t5.longitude
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables_1` t6 ON t2.bin = t6.bin

  SELECT 
    borough,
    manhattan_condominium_property_address,
    manhattan_condominium_property_boro_block_lot,
    manhattan_condominium_property_full_market_value,
    manhattan_condominium_property_total_units,
    manhattan_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft,
    SUM(manhattan_condominium_property_est_gross_income) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(manhattan_condominium_property_est_gross_income) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY 
    borough,
    manhattan_condominium_property_address,
    manhattan_condominium_property_boro_block_lot,
    manhattan_condominium_property_full_market_value,
    manhattan_condominium_property_total_units,
    manhattan_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft
)
SELECT 
  borough,
  manhattan_condominium_property_address,
  manhattan_condominium_property_boro_block_lot,
  manhattan_condominium_property_full_market_value,
  manhattan_condominium_property_total_units,
  manhattan_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE total > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

query: Can you show me, for each size category of water tank (small, medium, large), how many inspections there were, the average, total, and maximum tank count, broken down by whether the inspector noted any debris or insects, whether the tank passed the health standards, whether it was certified by the state, and whether the inspection was done by a private firm?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.si_req_debris_insects,
    t4.meet_standards,
    t5.tank_num,
    t6.nys_certified,
    t6.inspection_by_firm,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.tank_num > 50 THEN 'large_tank'
      WHEN t5.tank_num > 10 THEN 'medium_tank'
      ELSE 'small_tank'
    END AS category
  FROM `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.latitude = t2.latitude AND t1.longitude = t2.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_2` t3 ON t1.bin = t3.bin
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_3` t4 ON t1.inspection_date = t4.inspection_date
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections` t5 ON t1.block = t5.block
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_4` t6 ON t2.street_name = t6.street_name
  WHERE t4.meet_standards = 'Y'
)
SELECT 
  si_req_debris_insects,
  meet_standards,
  nys_certified,
  inspection_by_firm,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(tank_num) AS avg_value,
  SUM(tank_num) AS total_value,
  MAX(tank_num) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  si_req_debris_insects,
  meet_standards,
  nys_certified,
  inspection_by_firm,
  category

query: Can you show me the top 100 locations with the highest total number of water tanks where the most recent inspections passed, including both versions of the building ID, both versions of the block or area ID, the inspection dates used to match the records, whether the inspection standards were met, how many tanks that covers, the total and average number of tanks per location, and also any notes about required cleaning for debris or insects and the internal structural condition—making sure you only include records that haven’t been marked as removed or inactive?
sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.bin AS t1_bin,
    t3.bin AS t3_bin,
    t1.block AS t1_block,
    t5.block AS t5_block,
    t1.inspection_date AS t1_inspection_date,
    t4.inspection_date AS t4_inspection_date,
    t3.si_req_debris_insects,
    t4.meet_standards,
    t5.tank_num,
    t6.gi_result_internal_structure
  FROM `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.latitude = t2.latitude AND t1.longitude = t2.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_2` t3 ON t1.bin = t3.bin
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_3` t4 ON t1.inspection_date = t4.inspection_date
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections` t5 ON t1.block = t5.block
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_4` t6 ON t2.street_name = t6.street_name
  WHERE t5.deleted = 'No'
), aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    t1_bin,
    t3_bin,
    t1_block,
    t5_block,
    t1_inspection_date,
    t4_inspection_date,
    meet_standards,
    SUM(tank_num) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(tank_num) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY 
    t1_bin,
    t3_bin,
    t1_block,
    t5_block,
    t1_inspection_date,
    t4_inspection_date,
    meet_standards
)
SELECT 
  t1_bin,
  t3_bin,
  t1_block,
  t5_block,
  t1_inspection_date,
  t4_inspection_date,
  meet_standards,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE meet_standards = 'Y'
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

query: Could you show me, for each street that appears in both location references, which calendar year it falls under, whether an exterior inspection or special outside work was required, and if the tanks there passed the applicable health or safety standards—and along with that, give me the smallest, largest, average, and total number of tanks recorded for those streets, but only for situations where you’ve got at least a handful of inspections to base it on?
sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.street_name AS t2_street_name,
    t2.reporting_year,
    t3.gi_req_external_structure,
    t4.meet_standards,
    t5.tank_num,
    t6.street_name AS t6_street_name

  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections` t5 ON t1.block = t5.block
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_4` t6 ON t2.street_name = t6.street_name
  WHERE t2.reporting_year IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t2_street_name,
  t6_street_name,
  gi_req_external_structure,

query: Can you show me, for each street, the five most recent building water-tank inspections, including the building identifier, its approximate map location (latitude and longitude), the block it’s on, when the inspection took place, whether there were any issues with trash or insects, if the tank passed the inspection standards, whether E. coli was found, and whether the tank is certified by New York State?
sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.bin,
    t3.bin,
    t1.latitude,
    t2.longitude,
    t1.block,
    t5.block,
    t2.street_name,
    t6.street_name,
    t1.inspection_date,
    t4.inspection_date,
    t3.si_req_debris_insects,
    t4.meet_standards,
    t5.ecoli,
    t6.nys_certified,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t2.street_name ORDER BY t1.inspection_date DESC) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t6.street_name ORDER BY t4.inspection_date) AS dense_rank
  FROM `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.latitude = t2.latitude AND t1.longitude = t2.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_2` t3 ON t1.bin = t3.bin
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_3` t4 ON t1.inspection_date = t4.inspection_date
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections` t5 ON t1.block = t5.block
  INNER JOIN `Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_4` t6 ON t2.street_name = t6.street_name
)
SELECT 
  bin,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  block,
  street_name,
  inspection_date,
  si_req_debris_insects,
  meet_standards,
  ecoli,
  nys_certified,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5

query: Can you show me, for each type of facade filing in every city, how many records there are, what their average and total late penalties look like, and the highest late fee in each group, broken out by whether the filing is currently active, closed, or in some other status, and also indicate whether the penalties fall into low, medium, or high ranges?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t4.filing_type,
    t4.failure_to_file_amt,
    t5.sequence_no,
    t5.owner_city,
    t6.late_filing_amt,
    t6.current_status,
    CASE 
      WHEN t6.late_filing_amt > 15000 THEN 'High Penalty'
      WHEN t6.late_filing_amt > 5000 THEN 'Medium Penalty'
      ELSE 'Low Penalty'
    END as category
  FROM `node_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.tr6_no = t2.tr6_no
  INNER JOIN `DOB NOW： Safety – Facades Compliance Filings_facade_compliance_filings` t3 ON t1.control_no = t3.control_no
  INNER JOIN `DOB NOW： Safety – Facades Compliance Filings_facade_compliance_fines` t4 ON t1.bin = t4.bin
  INNER JOIN `DOB NOW： Safety – Facades Compliance Filings_facade_compliance_records` t5 ON t2.block = t5.block
  INNER JOIN `DOB NOW： Safety – Facades Compliance Filings_facade_compliance_records_1` t6 ON t3.house_no = t6.house_no
  WHERE t6.late_filing_amt IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  filing_type,
  owner_city,
  current_status,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(late_filing_amt) as avg_value,
  SUM(late_filing_amt) as total_value,
  MAX(late_filing_amt) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  filing_type,
  owner_city,
  current_status,
  category

WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT

    t3.charge_7_infraction_amount,
    t4.compliance_status,
    t4.balance_due,
    t6.scheduled_hearing_location,
    t6.paid_amount,
    CASE 
      WHEN t4.balance_due > 1000 THEN 'High balance'

  WHERE t6.violation_date IS NOT NULL

query: For each combination of respondent first name, respondent last name, and respondent house number, show how many violations fall into each payment-size category (low, medium, high) based on the paid amount, along with the average, total, and highest paid amount, using only records that have a violation date and are linked through the OATH Hearings Division Case Status hearing case details, hearing case status summary, and case status records tables.
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t6.respondent_first_name,
    t5.respondent_first_name,
    t1.respondent_address_house,
    t3.respondent_address_house,

  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.respondent_address_house = t3.respondent_address_house

  INNER JOIN `OATH Hearings Division Case Status_hearing_case_status_summary` t5 ON t2.respondent_address_street_name = t5.respondent_address_street_name
  INNER JOIN `OATH Hearings Division Case Status_oath_case_status_records` t6 ON t5.respondent_first_name = t6.respondent_first_name

)

SELECT t1.school_name, SUM(t6.attendance_rate) AS total_attendance_rate, t3.code1, t3.school_name, t6.code1, t4.fax_number, t1.fax_number FROM `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2019` t1
INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
INNER JOIN `node_4` t4 ON t1.fax_number = t4.fax_number
INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1` t6 ON t3.code1 = t6.code1 GROUP BY t1.school_name, t3.code1, t3.school_name, t6.code1, t4.fax_number, t1.fax_number

query: Can you show me the top 50 high school programs (by total attendance across all their records) where the average student attendance is above 90%, and for each one include the program’s identifying code, both listed contact phone numbers if they differ, how safe students report feeling there (as a percentage), and how many 9th‑grade applicants they received?
sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.code1,
    t2.phone_number,
    t5.phone_number AS t5_phone_number,
    t6.code1 AS t6_code1,
    t4.pct_stu_safe,
    t5.grade9geapplicants10,
    t6.attendance_rate
  FROM `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2019` t1
  INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN `node_4` t4 ON t1.fax_number = t4.fax_number
  INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
  INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1` t6 ON t3.code1 = t6.code1
  WHERE t6.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL
), aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    code1,
    phone_number,
    t5_phone_number,
    t6_code1,
    SUM(attendance_rate) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(attendance_rate) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY code1, phone_number, t5_phone_number, t6_code1
)
SELECT 
  code1,
  phone_number,
  t5_phone_number,
  t6_code1,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE average > 0.9
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 50

query: Could you show me the five most recent forestry service issues for each park area, including when each request was opened and closed, how it was ultimately resolved, a brief label for the type of issue, the latest time any details were updated, the full text of what the person reported, and which state the caller was from?

WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.parkzone,
    t3.closeddate,
    t4.createddate,
    t4.srresolution,
    t4.descriptor1,
    t5.updateddate,
    t5.complaintdetails,
    t5.callerstate,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.parkzone ORDER BY t4.createddate DESC) AS row_num
  FROM `Forestry Service Requests_forestry_service_requests` t1
  INNER JOIN `Forestry Service Requests_forestry_service_requests_3` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN `Forestry Service Requests_forestry_service_requests_2` t3 ON t1.globalid = t3.globalid

  parkzone,
  closeddate,
  createddate,
  srresolution,

  updateddate,
  complaintdetails,

query: Could you give me a breakdown of each high school and its program, showing how they’re grouped by attendance level (like high, medium, or low), along with how many records fall into each group and the average, total, and highest attendance for them? I’d also like that tied to each school’s main identifier and program code, plus any info you have on how many seats are offered and what percentage of students report feeling safe.
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.school_name, 
    t4.code1, 
    t1.code1, 
    t3.school_name AS t3_school_name, 
    t3.attendance_rate, 
    t4.seats109, 
    t5.pct_stu_safe,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.attendance_rate > 0.9 THEN 'High Attendance'
      WHEN t3.attendance_rate > 0.8 THEN 'Medium Attendance'
      ELSE 'Low Attendance'
    END as category
  FROM `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_information` t1
  INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_2` t4 ON t1.code1 = t4.code1
  INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
  WHERE t3.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  school_name, 
  code1, 
  t3_school_name, 
  category, 
  COUNT(*) as count, 
  AVG(attendance_rate) as avg_value, 
  SUM(attendance_rate) as total_value, 
  MAX(attendance_rate) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY school_name, code1, t3_school_name, category

query: Could you pull a summary of each high school, showing its official ID alongside any matching ID from the admissions records, the full school name from both sources if they differ, the main program or admissions code from each source, and the contact phone numbers that were used to link them? I’d also like to see each school’s attendance percentage, the specific admissions method or track used for that program, and how safe students reported feeling there, including overall counts and the minimum, maximum, and average of those safety ratings wherever attendance data is available.
sql:
WITH base_data AS (SELECT t1.dbn, t2.dbn AS t2_dbn, t1.school_name, t3.school_name AS t3_school_name, t1.code1, t4.code1 AS t4_code1, t2.phone_number, t5.phone_number AS t5_phone_number, t3.attendance_rate, t4.method4, t5.pct_stu_safe FROM `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_information` t1
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_2` t4 ON t1.code1 = t4.code1
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number WHERE t3.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL) SELECT dbn, t2_dbn, school_name, t3_school_name, code1, t4_code1, phone_number, t5_phone_number, COUNT(*) as record_count, SUM(pct_stu_safe) as total_amount, AVG(pct_stu_safe) as avg_amount, MAX(pct_stu_safe) as max_amount, MIN(pct_stu_safe) as min_amount FROM base_data GROUP BY dbn, t2_dbn, school_name, t3_school_name, code1, t4_code1, phone_number, t5_phone_number HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1

query: Can you show me, for the most recent five buildings in each project, the project name, when the building was finished, how many apartments it has in total, how many of those are two‑bedroom units, how many are reserved for middle‑income households and for any other income levels, along with an indication of whether the construction used prevailing-wage labor?

SELECT t3.prevailing_wage_status,
       t3.other_income_units,
       t3._2_br_units,
       t5.project_name,
       t5.total_units,
       t5.middle_income_units,
       t5.building_completion_date,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t5.project_name ORDER BY t5.building_completion_date DESC) AS row_num

query: Could you show me, for each building location, how many properties fall into each size group, along with the average, total, and largest number of housing units at that spot, especially focusing on places where the main counted units are available and comparing them with the units reserved for other income levels?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.latitude, 
    t1.longitude, 
    t3.latitude AS t3_latitude, 
    t3.longitude AS t3_longitude, 
    t1.all_counted_units, 
    t3.other_income_units, 
    t5.total_units,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.total_units > 100 THEN 'large'
      WHEN t5.total_units > 50 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'small'
    END AS category
  FROM `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_building_data_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_units_by_building` t2 ON t1.building_id = t2.building_id
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_building_data` t3 ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings_1` t4 ON t2.house_number = t4.house_number
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings` t5 ON t4.project_id = t5.project_id
  WHERE t1.all_counted_units IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t1_latitude AS latitude,
  t1_longitude AS longitude,
  category,

query: For each financial quarter since January 1, 2023, can you show me the top five park-cleaning days with the highest total hours worked, including the specific accounting day in the fiscal calendar, the actual work date, which sector of the park it was in, and the key staffing or task-related counts for that day (like number of workers assigned, crews on shift, and jobs completed)?
sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.fiscal_day,
    t2.fiscal_qtr,
    t3.nhours,
    t3.sector_name,
    t4.date_worked,
    t4.napsw,
    t5.ncpw,
    t5.njtp,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t2.fiscal_qtr ORDER BY t3.nhours DESC) AS row_num
  FROM `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_tasks_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_tasks_3` t2 ON t1.daily_task_activity_id = t2.daily_task_activity_id
  INNER JOIN `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_daily_tasks` t3 ON t1.row_id = t3.row_id
  INNER JOIN `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_tasks` t4 ON t1.daily_task_id = t4.daily_task_id
  INNER JOIN `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_tasks_2` t5 ON t1.propid = t5.propid
  WHERE t4.date_worked >= '2023-01-01'
)
SELECT 
  fiscal_qtr,
  fiscal_day,
  date_worked,
  sector_name,
  nhours,
  napsw,
  ncpw,
  njtp
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 5

query: Could you show me, for each individual park-cleaning activity and its related task and property, how many records fall into each shift-length category (short, medium, long), along with the average, total, and longest number of hours worked, plus the work date, the internal tracking codes for the activity and task, the property identifier, the fiscal day it falls under, and whatever that “ncpw” measure represents?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.daily_task_activity_id,
    t1.row_id,
    t1.daily_task_id,
    t1.propid,
    t2.fiscal_day,
    t3.nhours,
    t4.date_worked,
    t5.ncpw,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.nhours > 4 THEN 'Long shift'
      WHEN t3.nhours > 2 THEN 'Medium shift'
      ELSE 'Short shift'
    END as category
  FROM `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_tasks_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_tasks_3` t2 ON t1.daily_task_activity_id = t2.daily_task_activity_id
  INNER JOIN `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_daily_tasks` t3 ON t1.row_id = t3.row_id
  INNER JOIN `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_tasks` t4 ON t1.daily_task_id = t4.daily_task_id
  INNER JOIN `Daily Tasks Park Cleaning Records_park_cleaning_tasks_2` t5 ON t1.propid = t5.propid
  WHERE t4.date_worked IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  daily_task_activity_id,
  row_id,
  daily_task_id,
  propid,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(nhours) as avg_value,
  SUM(nhours) as total_value,
  MAX(nhours) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  daily_task_activity_id,
  row_id,
  daily_task_id,
  propid,
  category

query: For each DOB building code violation, show the DOB violation number, issue date, respondent city, and respondent house number, along with the ECB violation status and violation description. Group these by violation and classify each case into high, medium, or low penalty based on the penalty imposed, and for each group provide the count of records, and the average, total, and maximum penalty amounts.
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.dob_violation_number,
    t3.issue_date,
    t4.respondent_city,
    t5.respondent_house_number,
    t5.ecb_violation_status,
    t6.violation_description,
    t6.penality_imposed,
    CASE 
      WHEN t6.penality_imposed > 10000 THEN 'High Penalty'
      WHEN t6.penality_imposed > 1000 THEN 'Medium Penalty'
      ELSE 'Low Penalty'
    END as category
  FROM `DOB ECB Violations_dob_ecb_violation_records_3` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOB ECB Violations_dob_ecb_violation_records_1` t2 ON t1.ecb_violation_number = t2.ecb_violation_number
  INNER JOIN `DOB ECB Violations_dob_ecb_violation_records_2` t3 ON t1.dob_violation_number = t3.dob_violation_number
  INNER JOIN `DOB ECB Violations_respondent_address_info` t4 ON t1.respondent_name = t4.respondent_name
  INNER JOIN `DOB ECB Violations_dob_ecb_violation_records` t5 ON t1.bin = t5.bin
  INNER JOIN `DOB ECB Violations_building_violation_records` t6 ON t2.block = t6.block
  WHERE t6.penality_imposed IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  dob_violation_number,
  issue_date,
  respondent_city,
  ecb_violation_status,
  violation_description,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(penality_imposed) as avg_value,
  SUM(penality_imposed) as total_value,
  MAX(penality_imposed) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  dob_violation_number,
  issue_date,
  respondent_city,
  ecb_violation_status,
  violation_description,
  category

query: For each city where ACS Community Partners programs operate, show the number of distinct program codes and the total of all program contact fax numbers recorded in the community partner office hours data, then list the top 50 cities ordered by the highest total fax activity.
sql:

INNER JOIN `ACS Community Partners_community_programs_ny` t4 ON t1.program_name = t4.program_name

query: Could you show me a list of the top active community programs, including their unique program IDs, any internal program codes, the program names, and their primary street addresses along with the city and zip code? I’d also like to see their exact map coordinates (latitude and longitude), the last name and phone number of the main contact person, and the usual Wednesday opening time. Finally, please include their Saturday office hours (when they open and close on Saturdays) and make sure only programs that are currently active are included.
sql:
WITH raw_data AS (SELECT t1.program_lst_id, t1.program_code, t1.program_name, t1.program_address_1, t1.latitude, t1.longitude, t1.prog_contact_last_name, t1.prog_contact_phone_no, t2.program_zip, t3.program_code AS t3_program_code, t4.program_name AS t4_program_name, t4.program_city, t5.program_address_1 AS t5_program_address_1, t5.office_wed_from_time, t6.latitude AS t6_latitude, t6.longitude AS t6_longitude, t6.active_flag, t7.prog_contact_last_name AS t7_prog_contact_last_name, t7.office_sat_to_time, t8.prog_contact_phone_no AS t8_prog_contact_phone_no, t8.office_sat_from_time FROM `ACS Community Partners_community_program_locations` t1
INNER JOIN `ACS Community Partners_community_program_offices` t2 ON t1.program_lst_id = t2.program_lst_id
INNER JOIN `ACS Community Partners_community_program_bbl_mapping` t3 ON t1.program_code = t3.program_code
INNER JOIN `ACS Community Partners_community_programs_ny` t4 ON t1.program_name = t4.program_name
INNER JOIN `ACS Community Partners_community_partner_locations_1` t5 ON t1.program_address_1 = t5.program_address_1
INNER JOIN `ACS Community Partners_community_partner_locations` t6 ON t1.latitude = t6.latitude AND t1.longitude = t6.longitude
INNER JOIN `ACS Community Partners_community_partner_office_hours` t7 ON t1.prog_contact_last_name = t7.prog_contact_last_name
INNER JOIN `node_8` t8 ON t1.prog_contact_phone_no = t8.prog_contact_phone_no WHERE t6.active_flag = 'Y'), filtered AS (SELECT program_city, program_zip, office_sat_from_time, office_sat_to_time, program_name, program_address_1, latitude, longitude FROM raw_data WHERE office_sat_from_time IS NOT NULL AND office_sat_to_time IS NOT NULL), aggregated AS (SELECT program_city, COUNT(*) as count, SUM(program_zip) as total FROM filtered GROUP BY program_city) SELECT program_city, count, total FROM aggregated ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 50

query: Can you show me, for each state, the five most recent permits issued since the start of 2021, including where the load ended (city and ZIP), the model year of the truck, how heavy the load was in total, and how wide it was?
sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT t3.trailerstate,
         t3.endzipcode,
         t3.truckyear,
         t3.totalgrossweight,
         t5.applicationdate,
         t5.endcity,
         t5.overallwidth,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.trailerstate ORDER BY t5.applicationdate DESC) AS row_num
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
  WHERE t5.applicationdate >= '2021-01-01'
)
SELECT trailerstate,
       endzipcode,
       truckyear,
       totalgrossweight,
       applicationdate,
       endcity,
       overallwidth
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 5

query: Could you show me, for each permit number, how many trips fall into each weight category (Standard, Heavy, Very Heavy), along with the average, total, and maximum overall vehicle weight for those trips, but only for permits where the vehicle was wider than 8 feet?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT t1.fullpermitno, t3.fullpermitno, t1.loadweight, t3.totalgrossweight, t5.overallwidth,
         CASE
           WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 160000 THEN 'Very Heavy'
           WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 120000 THEN 'Heavy'
           ELSE 'Standard'
         END AS category
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
  WHERE t5.overallwidth > 8.0
)
SELECT fullpermitno, category, COUNT(*) AS count,
       AVG(totalgrossweight) AS avg_value,
       SUM(totalgrossweight) AS total_value,
       MAX(totalgrossweight) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY fullpermitno, category

query: Can you show me the top five permits in each trailer’s home state with the greatest vehicle width, including where each trip ended (city and ZIP), where it started (state and ZIP), when the permit was applied for, how old the truck was at the time, and how they stack up against others both within the trailer’s state and the starting state?
sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.trailerstate,
    t3.endzipcode,
    t3.truckyear,
    t4.applicationdate,
    t4.startzipcode,
    t4.startstate,
    t5.applicationdate,
    t5.endcity,
    t5.overallwidth,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.trailerstate 
      ORDER BY t5.overallwidth DESC
    ) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t4.startstate 
      ORDER BY t3.truckyear
    ) AS dense_rank
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
)
SELECT 
  trailerstate,
  endzipcode,
  truckyear,
  applicationdate,
  startzipcode,
  startstate,
  endcity,
  overallwidth,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5

query: Can you show me the most recent five permits issued since the start of 2023, including the permit number, the dates they were applied for, how heavy the load was, the total weight of the vehicle plus the load, the length and height of the load, and the city where each trip was supposed to end?

query: Could you show me, for each permit application and its matching reference number, the original and linked application dates, the state where the trailer was registered, the destination city, and how many moves fall into each weight category, along with the average, total, and heaviest overall loaded weight for those moves?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.fullapplicationno AS t2_fullapplicationno,
    t4.fullapplicationno,
    t4.applicationdate,
    t5.applicationdate AS t5_applicationdate,
    t3.trailerstate,
    t5.endcity,
    t3.totalgrossweight,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 160000 THEN 'very_heavy'
      WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 120000 THEN 'heavy'
      ELSE 'standard'
    END AS category
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
  WHERE t3.totalgrossweight IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t2_fullapplicationno,
  fullapplicationno,
  applicationdate,
  t5_applicationdate,
  trailerstate,
  endcity,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(totalgrossweight) AS avg_value,
  SUM(totalgrossweight) AS total_value,
  MAX(totalgrossweight) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  t2_fullapplicationno,
  fullapplicationno,
  applicationdate,
  t5_applicationdate,
  trailerstate,
  endcity,
  category

INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno

query: Could you pull a list of the top 100 city and state combinations for oversize vehicle permits issued since the start of 2023, showing how many permits went through each city, the total combined width of those loads, and the average width per permit?
sql:
WITH base_data AS (
SELECT 
  t1.permitid,
  t1.fullpermitno,
  t2.permitid AS t2_permitid,
  t2.fullapplicationno,
  t4.fullapplicationno AS t4_fullapplicationno,
  t4.applicationdate,
  t3.fullpermitno AS t3_fullpermitno,
  t3.trailerstate,
  t5.applicationdate,
  t5.endcity,
  t5.overallwidth
FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
WHERE t5.applicationdate >= '2023-01-01') ,
aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    trailerstate,
    endcity,
    SUM(overallwidth) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(overallwidth) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY trailerstate, endcity
)
SELECT 
  trailerstate,
  endcity,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE count >= 1
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

query: Could you show me, for each school, the top five cases where students report feeling the safest and most respected, along with how engaged they say their teachers are with students’ future goals, how well students feel they can communicate, the school’s name, how safe and respected parents feel there, how effective teacher communication is rated, who the principal is, and whether it’s, for example, an elementary, middle, or high school?

query: Could you show me, for each school, the different engagement categories and how many students fall into each one, along with the average, total, and highest engagement score for those students, plus the type of school and any related reference IDs that were used to link the communication and engagement information between students and teachers?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t1.school_name, t1.unnamed_column, t3.unnamed_column, t4.school_name, t3.student_communication_score, t4.teacher_communication_score, t1.student_engagement_score, t5.school_type, CASE WHEN t1.student_engagement_score > 8 THEN 'High engagement' WHEN t1.student_engagement_score > 6 THEN 'Medium engagement' ELSE 'Low engagement' END as category FROM `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_1` t1
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_2009` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores` t3 ON t1.unnamed_column = t3.unnamed_column
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_performance_scores` t4 ON t1.school_name = t4.school_name
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_transfer_school_principals_2009` t5 ON t2.principal = t5.principal WHERE t5.school_type IS NOT NULL) SELECT school_name, school_type, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(student_engagement_score) as avg_value, SUM(student_engagement_score) as total_value, MAX(student_engagement_score) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY school_name, school_type, category

query: Could you show me, for each school, the different engagement or program categories they have, the corresponding codes or identifiers for those categories, the name of the principal in charge, and the total combined score for how well students communicate or participate in those areas?
sql:
SELECT t1.school_name, t1.unnamed_column, t3.unnamed_column, t4.school_name, t5.principal, SUM(t3.student_communication_score) AS total_student_communication_score FROM `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_1` t1
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_2009` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores` t3 ON t1.unnamed_column = t3.unnamed_column
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_performance_scores` t4 ON t1.school_name = t4.school_name
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_transfer_school_principals_2009` t5 ON t2.principal = t5.principal GROUP BY t1.school_name, t1.unnamed_column, t3.unnamed_column, t4.school_name, t5.principal

query: Could you show me, by type of school, which principals are leading schools where students feel most engaged overall, and also feel that communication with students and teachers is strong and that parents see the school as safe and respectful—with the results limited to school types that have enough responses to make the comparisons meaningful?
sql: WITH base_data AS (SELECT t2.principal, t5.principal AS t5_principal, t5.school_type, t2.engagement_score, t3.student_communication_score, t4.teacher_communication_score, t4.parent_safety_and_respect FROM `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_1` t1 INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_2009` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores` t3 ON t1.unnamed_column = t3.unnamed_column INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_performance_scores` t4 ON t1.school_name = t4.school_name INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_transfer_school_principals_2009` t5 ON t2.principal = t5.principal WHERE t2.engagement_score IS NOT NULL), aggregated AS (SELECT school_type, SUM(engagement_score) as total, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(engagement_score) as average FROM base_data GROUP BY school_type) SELECT school_type, total, count, average FROM aggregated WHERE count >= 5 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 50

query: Could you show me, for each school leader, who was in charge originally and who took over later, along with the total score of how well students felt they could communicate and the average score of how well teachers were rated on their communication?
sql:
SELECT t5.principal AS principal_t5, t2.principal AS principal_t2, SUM(t3.student_communication_score) AS total_dimension1, AVG(t4.teacher_communication_score) AS average_dimension2 FROM `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_1` t1
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_2009` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores` t3 ON t1.unnamed_column = t3.unnamed_column
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_performance_scores` t4 ON t1.school_name = t4.school_name
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_transfer_school_principals_2009` t5 ON t2.principal = t5.principal GROUP BY t5.principal, t2.principal

query: For each school and its campus or program code, can you show me the school’s name, the principal’s name, how students rate communication at the school, how teachers rate communication, and the corresponding student engagement level, along with how many records you have for each combination, plus the total, average, highest, and lowest engagement values for that group?
sql: WITH base_data AS (SELECT t1.dbn, t1.unnamed_column, t2.dbn, t1.school_name, t5.principal, t4.school_name, t3.unnamed_column, t2.principal, t3.student_communication_score, t4.teacher_communication_score, t2.engagement_score FROM `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_1` t1 INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_2009` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores` t3 ON t1.unnamed_column = t3.unnamed_column INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_performance_scores` t4 ON t1.school_name = t4.school_name INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_transfer_school_principals_2009` t5 ON t2.principal = t5.principal WHERE t2.engagement_score IS NOT NULL) SELECT dbn, unnamed_column, school_name, principal, engagement_score, COUNT(*) as record_count, SUM(engagement_score) as total_amount, AVG(engagement_score) as avg_amount, MAX(engagement_score) as max_amount, MIN(engagement_score) as min_amount FROM base_data GROUP BY dbn, unnamed_column, school_name, principal, engagement_score HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1

query: Could you list each school along with its unique school code, the name of the person in charge, the kind of school it is (for example, whether it’s a particular category or program type), and the total combined student engagement score for that school?

SELECT t1.dbn, t1.school_name, t2.principal, t5.school_type, SUM(t2.engagement_score) AS total_engagement_score FROM `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_1` t1
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores_2009` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `2009 Public Data File Students_student_engagement_scores` t3 ON t1.unnamed_column = t3.unnamed_column

query: Can you show me up to five of the most recently listed women’s service locations in Brooklyn, including whether they also serve Staten Island, any health-related support they provide, the street address, whether the listing is marked as currently active, and what they offer for older women and for those dealing with domestic violence?
sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.staten_island,
    t3.health,
    t4.brooklyn,
    t4.published,
    t4.address2,
    t5.aging,
    t5.domestic_violence,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t4.brooklyn ORDER BY t4.address2 DESC) AS row_num
  FROM `NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_services_info` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_organizations_info` t2 ON t1.organizationname = t2.organizationname
  INNER JOIN `NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_resources` t3 ON t1.address1 = t3.address1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_resources_1` t4 ON t1.phone = t4.phone
  INNER JOIN `NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_services_locations` t5 ON t2.location_1 = t5.location_1
  WHERE t4.published = 'Published'
)
SELECT 
  staten_island,
  health,
  brooklyn,
  published,
  address2,
  aging,
  domestic_violence
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 5

query: Can you break down Brooklyn condo rentals by neighborhood and show, for each section of a building and specific property (using whatever ID you have along with the street address), how much income they bring in per square foot and their total floor area—and then group those places into low, medium, and high income-per-square-foot bands, with counts, averages, totals, and the highest value in each band for every neighborhood?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.brooklyn_condominium_property_condo_section,
    t3.brooklyn_condominium_property_address,
    t4.brooklyn_condominium_property_boro_block_lot,
    t5.brooklyn_condominium_property_gross_sqft,
    t6.brooklyn_condominium_property_neighborhood,
    t4.brooklyn_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft,
    CASE 
      WHEN t4.brooklyn_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft > 30 THEN 'high'
      WHEN t4.brooklyn_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft > 15 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'low'
    END as category
  FROM `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Brooklyn - FY 2010 2011_brooklyn_condo_rental_data` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Brooklyn - FY 2010 2011_brooklyn_condo_rental_comparables` t2 ON t1.brooklyn_condominium_property_condo_section = t2.brooklyn_condominium_property_condo_section
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Brooklyn - FY 2010 2011_brooklyn_condo_rental_comparables_1` t3 ON t1.brooklyn_condominium_property_address = t3.brooklyn_condominium_property_address
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Brooklyn - FY 2010 2011_brooklyn_condo_rental_income` t4 ON t1.brooklyn_condominium_property_boro_block_lot = t4.brooklyn_condominium_property_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Brooklyn - FY 2010 2011_brooklyn_condo_rental_comparisons` t5 ON t1.latitude = t5.latitude AND t1.longitude = t5.longitude
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Brooklyn - FY 2010 2011_brooklyn_condo_rental_comparables_2` t6 ON t1.bin = t6.bin
  WHERE t4.brooklyn_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  brooklyn_condominium_property_neighborhood,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(brooklyn_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft) as avg_value,
  SUM(brooklyn_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft) as total_value,
  MAX(brooklyn_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY brooklyn_condominium_property_neighborhood, category

query: Could you show me, by area and by the range of grades a school serves, how many schools fall into each performance level based on how many of their students pass their classes, and for each of those groups also include the average, highest, and total pass rates? I’d also like that broken out by whether they have specialized support for students learning English, and limited to schools where those pass‑rate numbers are actually reported.
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t2.neighborhood, t3.gradespan, t4.ellprograms, t5.overview, t6.othersports, t4.coursepassrate, CASE WHEN t4.coursepassrate > 90 THEN 'High performance' WHEN t4.coursepassrate > 70 THEN 'Medium performance' ELSE 'Low performance' END as category FROM `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_directory` t1
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_admissions_info` t2 ON t1.schooldbn = t2.schooldbn
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.name = t3.name
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_admissions_data` t4 ON t1.code_prog1 = t4.code_prog1
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_programs` t5 ON t1.telephone = t5.telephone
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_programs_info` t6 ON t1.name_prog1 = t6.name_prog1 WHERE t4.coursepassrate IS NOT NULL) SELECT neighborhood, gradespan, ellprograms, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(coursepassrate) as avg_value, SUM(coursepassrate) as total_value, MAX(coursepassrate) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY neighborhood, gradespan, ellprograms, category

query: I’m trying to find the top 50 middle schools with the strongest overall student course performance. Could you list the schools with the highest combined course pass rates, along with each school’s name, the area or neighborhood it’s in, a brief description of the school, the range of grades it serves, a summary of how well students are passing their classes on average, how many course records that average is based on, and any other sports or extracurricular sports programs they offer?
sql:
WITH base_data AS (SELECT t3.name, t1.name, t1.name_prog1, t1.code_prog1, t2.schooldbn, t5.telephone, t4.code_prog1, t1.schooldbn, t1.telephone, t6.name_prog1, t2.neighborhood, t3.gradespan, t4.coursepassrate, t5.overview, t6.othersports FROM `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_directory` t1
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_admissions_info` t2 ON t1.schooldbn = t2.schooldbn
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.name = t3.name
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_admissions_data` t4 ON t1.code_prog1 = t4.code_prog1
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_programs` t5 ON t1.telephone = t5.telephone
INNER JOIN `2021 DOE Middle School Directory_middle_school_programs_info` t6 ON t1.name_prog1 = t6.name_prog1 WHERE t4.coursepassrate IS NOT NULL), aggregated AS (SELECT name, neighborhood, SUM(coursepassrate) as total, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(coursepassrate) as average FROM base_data GROUP BY name, neighborhood) SELECT name, neighborhood, total, count, average FROM aggregated WHERE count >= 1 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 50

query: For the 2016–17 school year, can you show me, for each enrollment group, the top three groups with the highest average number of property-related incidents, along with their average counts of other kinds of incidents, average non-criminal incidents, how many schools are in each group, the total number of non-criminal incidents reported, and how many students were enrolled?
sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.engroupa,
    t3.avgofoth_n,
    t3.avgofnocrim_n,
    t3.avgofprop_n,
    t3.schools,
    t5.school_year,
    t5.nocrim_n,
    t5.register,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.engroupa ORDER BY t3.avgofprop_n DESC) AS row_num
  FROM `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_statistics` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.location_name = t2.location_name
  INNER JOIN `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_metrics` t3 ON t1.location_code = t3.location_code
  INNER JOIN `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_incidents` t4 ON t2.geocode = t4.geocode
  INNER JOIN `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_data` t5 ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
  WHERE t5.school_year = '2016 - 17'
)
SELECT 
  engroupa,
  avgofoth_n,
  avgofnocrim_n,
  avgofprop_n,
  schools,
  school_year,
  nocrim_n,
  register
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 3

query: For each type of school or student group, can you show me, by school year, the total, average, and number of records for that property‑related safety measure so I can compare how it changes over time across the different groups?

SELECT t3.engroupa, t5.school_year, SUM(t3.avgofprop_n) AS total, AVG(t3.avgofprop_n) AS average, COUNT(*) AS count FROM `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_statistics` t1

query: For each school location in 2016–17, can you list the different area codes you’re using to identify the place, the two sets of coordinates you have on record for it, and then summarize how many incidents there were in total, on average, and at the highest level, broken out by your low/medium/high safety categories?
sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.geocode,
    t4.geocode AS t4_geocode,
    t4.latitude,
    t4.longitude,
    t5.latitude AS t5_latitude,
    t5.longitude AS t5_longitude,
    t3.avgofprop_n,
    t5.nocrim_n,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.nocrim_n > 10 THEN 'high'
      WHEN t5.nocrim_n > 5 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'low'
    END as category
  FROM `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_statistics` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.location_name = t2.location_name
  INNER JOIN `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_metrics` t3 ON t1.location_code = t3.location_code
  INNER JOIN `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_incidents` t4 ON t2.geocode = t4.geocode
  INNER JOIN `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_data` t5 ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
  WHERE t5.school_year = '2016 - 17'
)
SELECT 
  geocode,
  t4_geocode,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  t5_latitude,
  t5_longitude,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(nocrim_n) as avg_value,
  SUM(nocrim_n) as total_value,
  MAX(nocrim_n) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  geocode,
  t4_geocode,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  t5_latitude,
  t5_longitude,
  category

INNER JOIN `Use of ARRA Stimulus Funds_arra_stimulus_fund_usage_1` t3 ON t1.contract_id_ = t3.contract_id_
